literal.prompt: Как называется переход снега или льда прямо в водяной пар?

literalGroups.primaryGround: NSIDC says sublimation in very dry Antarctica can make glaciers disappear and defines it as solids transitioning directly to gas. The other choices name different glacier processes: calving breaks off ice chunks; firn forms from compressed snow; ablation is a seasonal mass-loss process. Only sublimation matches ice/snow directly becoming vapor.
literalGroups.locator: NSIDC Science of Glaciers L67,L72,L84,L108; Science of Ice Shelves L75

literalGroups.literal: Это сублимация. Процесс удаляет массу с ледяной поверхности без образования талой воды.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NSIDC L67 says solids transition directly to gas and that Antarctic glaciers can disappear because of sublimation. The explanation’s no-liquid inference follows from that phase definition; it does not claim that all polar ice loss occurs this way.

literalGroups.literal: Кальвинг — отделение глыб льда от фронта ледника или шельфа.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NSIDC L67 directly defines solid-to-gas transition and says Antarctic glaciers may disappear because of sublimation.

literalGroups.literal: В очень сухих районах Антарктиды сублимация может приводить к исчезновению ледников.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The note defines calving as chunks breaking off the seaward edge of an ice shelf; NSIDC also says tidewater glaciers calve icebergs. This is a credible cryosphere distractor, but it names detachment of solid ice rather than a phase change to vapor.
literalGroups.locator: NSIDC Science of Ice Shelves L75; Science of Glaciers L155

literalGroups.literal: Фирнизация превращает многолетний снег в зернистый фирн, а затем в ледниковый лёд.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NSIDC says snow surviving a melt season becomes denser, compressed firn and that snow and firn are further compressed into glacier ice. Firnization is a plausible snow/ice process but describes compaction into firn/ice, not direct vapor transition.

literalGroups.literal: Абляция — совокупная потеря массы ледником из-за таяния, испарения и откалывания.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The note accurately summarizes glacier mass-loss processes; NSIDC describes melting, evaporation and calving as losses and identifies ablation as a natural seasonal part of glacier life, with melting/evaporation concentrated in lower ablation areas. Ablation is broader glacier mass-balance language, not the particular solid-to-vapor transition asked for.

correctNoteNewFact.fact: In very dry parts of Antarctica, glaciers may grow slowly or even disappear because of sublimation.

absoluteDifficulty.audience: Broad adult audience with general school science knowledge.
absoluteDifficulty.basis: The prompt itself states the defining phase transition in plain language; sublimation is a standard school-science term. It is one-step identification, not a specialist glaciology inference. The options are related but distinct cryosphere processes, not absurd giveaways.
